analysis:
Examined EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (base 544-953 and head 1-539). Changes: (1) the nonthrowing submitTokenized overload (head 89-93) now also catches MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError.unsupportedOutputControl and yields its content-free marker in-band; (2) a new early check in the throwing overload (head 150-154) calls nativeOutputControlRefusal(request:tokenConstraint:) after the canSubmitWithNativeOwner guard and before duplicate-ID, service allowance, calibration, cache receipts, SSD staging and KV reservation; (3) a helper is added near line 960, but its body is truncated in the patch, so I could not read it.

Security assessment: the new refusal path runs before any resources are acquired (no service allowance, no pendingSubmissionIDs insert, no prefix receipts, no staging, no shared KV), so there is no leak or unbalanced release. It calls usageSignal?.finalizeLookup(failure: .policy, ...) and continuation.finish() before throwing, which is consistent with the other pre-reservation refusals (head 176-198). The marker is a fixed content-free string, with no prompt data in the error. This reduces the chance of an SDK-internal error crashing or hanging a request, so it is a fail-closed change. It does not touch encryption (T-008), the cache scope or SSD gating (T-041), or attestation.

Remaining questions for integration: (a) nativeOutputControlRefusal's body and its message contents are not visible, so content-freeness of the message cannot be confirmed; (b) callers of the nonthrowing overload must map the marker back to a typed error; (c) whether the throwing overload's callers handle unsupportedOutputControl, which is outside the supplied evidence. The rest of the file's cache, deadline, retirement and SSD staging code is unchanged in this diff, so I did not re-audit it.
